text:
alex: seeing a sudden p95 latency spike (~2.1x) for model-rx on cluster-gamma starting 09:12 UTC. dashboards show tail tokens stalling. link: https://dash.redwood/runtime/cluster-gamma
maria: ugh. any correlation with deployments or autoscale?
alex: no deploys. CPU steal spiked on node pool-a, and kernel selection counts show a jump to 'generic-matmul' for long sequences. suspect wrong kernel choice for seq>1024.
tim: can you attach a perf record? also K/V cache evictions have a large sweep trace around the same time.
alex: pasting flamegraph (trimmed):
```
  flamegraph: hotpath -> aten::matmul -> generic_matmul_kernel
  hot frames: generic_matmul_kernel + 48%
  note: optimized_kernel_v2 shows <5%
```
maria: that aligns with the kernel selector fallback kicking in. we shipped a micro-heuristic last week that prefers generic kernel for safety on mixed-precision. maybe it's mis-triggering on certain batch/seq mixes.
dave: looks like a noisy-tenant effect too: one tenant sent a burst of long-seq infer calls that filled KV cache metadata and caused eviction sweeps, which bumped CPU scheduling.
 alex: i captured a quick profile and kv eviction log: `kvcache: evict sweep 3.2s, freed 0 entries, scanned 14k`
tim: ok mitigation proposals: 1) emergency throttle on requests with seq>1024 for non-prod tenants, 2) flip feature flag to disable the last-week kernel heuristic, 3) temporarily route long-seq to fallback nodes with optimized kernel pinned.
maria: +1 to feature flag. can we toggle without restart?
dave: yes — feature flags are dynamic. flag name: `runtime.use_safe_generic_kernel` -> currently true. toggling to false should prefer optimized kernel paths.
alex: test on canary: `curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/flags/runtime.use_safe_generic_kernel -d '{"value":false}'`
deploy-bot: deploy event: FLAG_UPDATE runtime.use_safe_generic_kernel=false by maria @ 09:27 UTC :white_check_mark:
sre-bot: Incident PERF-2026-0312-07 created. severity: S2. runbook: Runtime kernel misselection / KV eviction noisy-tenant.
 tim: started a small routing rule to send seq>2048 to fallback-pool (optimized-kernels) for tenant set X,Y at 09:30 UTC.
maria: also put a short-term throttle: `rate_limit.long_seq_burst: 20rps` for public api at 09:31.
alex: after flag flip + routing, p95 dropped back to baseline within ~3 minutes. metrics: p95 before=320ms, during=640ms, after=340ms.
dave: KV eviction sweeps also reduced, eviction-duration 3.2s -> 0.6s. likely less churn.
tim: follow-ups: - revert or refine kernel heuristic (investigate corner case where mixed-precision + batch packing toggles weights layout) - add selector telemetry to emit decision factors (seq_len, batch_size, dtype) - add tenant burst protection for long-seq requests
maria: I'll open a backlog ticket for the heuristic rewrite and add an eval harness to reproduce. assigning to eng-runtime/kernel-team.
 alex: notes for postmortem: short incident (~20m impact), root cause: heuristic mis-trigger on certain seq/batch combos + tenant burst causing KV eviction churn -> CPU scheduling impact -> latency spike. mitigations enacted: feature flag flip, routing to fallback, throttle.
dave: leaving the incident open until kernel-team writes a patch and we validate canary.
maria: thanks everyone. nice quick coordination. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Incident update: FLAG_UPDATE rollback scheduled? none.
sre-bot: Incident PERF-2026-0312-07 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
alex: attaching profiler + minimal repro steps in the ticket.
maria: please @kernel-team when ready for canary patch review.
 tim: logging action items in #eng-runtime-ops board.
dave: closing thread here, moving discussion to the ticket for the long term.
